conclusion: C/C is the common genotype at rs117385980 (SIRT6 c.194+194G>A) and carries no copy of the T allele; about 95% of Europeans and effectively all East Asians are C/C. Two independent cohorts found the T allele less often among the longest-lived. Hirvonen 2017 (Finnish men, n=198 combined) saw T carriage in 9/92 men who had died at a mean age of 66.6 y versus 1/43 healthy long-lived men and 2/63 healthy men of mean age 83 y (OR 3.58, 95% CI 0.96-13.4, p=0.074). Sheikholmolouki 2025 (Birjand, Iran, n=227, both sexes) found the T allele in 4/288 alleles at 60-69 y, 4/86 at 70-79 y and 0/80 at 80-90 y (p=0.073). This genotype is labelled 'protective' only as the relative direction of that trend; it is the population norm, not a prediction of long life. Neither cohort reached statistical significance and no individual risk estimate can be derived from either. Note on annotation: the source article describes rs117385980 as a stop-gained variant in SIRT6 exon 2. That is not supportable. On the MANE Select transcript NM_016539.4 / ENST00000337491 the variant is c.194+194G>A, 194 bp inside intron 2, and Ensembl VEP returns intron_variant for every SIRT6 transcript. The p.Trp38Ter prediction in dbSNP comes from one Gnomon-predicted RefSeq model transcript (XM_024451539.2) whose exon 2 is longer than any curated transcript's. The variant also sits inside an AluSx4 repeat (chr19:4,180,385-4,180,624). Treat it as a non-coding marker, not as a loss-of-function allele.

T/T at rs107251 (SIRT6 c.438-151A>G, intronic) was the genotype with the shortest observed life in TenNapel 2014, a molecular epidemiological study of 1,192 genotyped members of the Iowa 65+ Rural Health Study (European ancestry, enrolled at age 65 or over, age at death as a continuous outcome). Adjusted mean age at death was 5.5 years lower than C/C and 5.9 years lower than T/C (q=0.012); unadjusted means were 82.1 y for T/T against 87.6 y (C/C) and 88.0 y (T/C). Two strong caveats: the estimate rests on only 10 T/T individuals out of 1,192, and the cohort was recruited at 65+, so genotypes that shorten life before 65 are under-represented by construction. The authors themselves note rs107251 is not in a mammalian conserved region and is unlikely to be causal. Orientation warning: on GRCh38 the reference base at rs107251 is T, and T is the global minor allele (gnomAD v4 frequency 0.116). The genotype associated with shorter life in TenNapel 2014 is therefore the homozygous *reference* genotype. Do not infer direction from ref/alt status. rs117385980, rs107251 and rs350846 are not independent signals: in 1000 Genomes EUR all three sit on one haplotype (D' = 1.00 pairwise; r2 = 0.30 between rs117385980 and each of the other two, limited only by the frequency difference). The three published associations may be one signal seen through three markers.

No direction is asserted for C/C at rs350846 (SIRT6 c.*216G>C, 3'UTR). You/Li 2016 studied 169 long-lived people aged 90-110 in Bama County, China against two control sets, and its abstract concludes that the C allele and the C/C and C/G genotypes are 'associated with longevity'. Its own Table 4 does not support that reading: C allele frequency was 28.7% in the longevity group, 27.8% in the internal controls (p=0.796, OR 1.046) and 38.6% in the external controls (p=0.006, OR 0.639, i.e. C *lower* in the long-lived). The two control groups differed from each other more than the long-lived differed from either (p=0.003), so the significant result is a discrepancy between control sets, not a longevity signal. Direction left unknown deliberately. rs117385980, rs107251 and rs350846 are not independent signals: in 1000 Genomes EUR all three sit on one haplotype (D' = 1.00 pairwise; r2 = 0.30 between rs117385980 and each of the other two, limited only by the frequency difference). The three published associations may be one signal seen through three markers.

No direction is asserted for C/G at rs350846 (SIRT6 c.*216G>C, 3'UTR). In You/Li 2016 (Bama County, China) C/G was seen in 63/169 long-lived people aged 90-110, 59/158 internal controls and 88/176 external controls; the long-lived and internal control groups did not differ (p=0.841) and the only significant contrasts involved the external control group, which also differed from the internal control group (p=0.004). The published conclusion that C-carrying genotypes favour longevity is not supported by the paper's own allele table, which puts C lower in the long-lived than in the external controls. rs117385980, rs107251 and rs350846 are not independent signals: in 1000 Genomes EUR all three sit on one haplotype (D' = 1.00 pairwise; r2 = 0.30 between rs117385980 and each of the other two, limited only by the frequency difference). The three published associations may be one signal seen through three markers.
